blindSummary: No region-specific law, incident series or enforcement finding was identified for this unit in the dedicated country dossier; regional LGBTI or equality legislation is recorded in the national policy inventories, but no sub-national facility, expression or assembly restriction exists anywhere in the country, and the 2023 national trans-equality law's implementation (including its education-facing parts) falls to this unit's government. Victimisation figures for this unit follow the national picture: a 2026 report found 44% of LGBTI respondents had experienced a hate-motivated incident.
blindSourceSummaries: Official state-gazette publication of the 2023 trans-equality law (published 1 March 2023): the national trans-equality law whose administrative and education-facing provisions are implemented by each state/province - the framework this region applies.

International human-rights organisation news release (16 February 2023) welcoming the country's new gender-recognition law: legal gender recognition by self-declaration from age 12 under certain conditions without medical diagnosis, placing the country among the earliest autonomy-first jurisdictions in the world (with a handful of peer countries); frames diagnostic and sterilisation requirements elsewhere as rights violations.

Criminal-defence law-firm analysis (June 2026, updated September 2026) disentangling three frequently conflated statutes: the 2023 trans-equality law is an ordinary statute that never amended the criminal code (its content is civil, administrative, health, employment and educational); the discrimination aggravating factor and the hate-offences provisions in the criminal code come from a 2022 reform (hate offences: 1 to 4 years' imprisonment plus a 6-12 month fine); 'gender expression' appears in no article of the criminal code.
